title: Influence of cross-modal load on cognitive processing and decision-making
titleZh: 跨通道负荷对认知加工与决策的影响
abstract: Abstract Thoughtful design of multitask scenarios alleviates some competition for limited attentional resources. However, tasks that demand separate perceptual resources may still result in processing overload. In this experiment, participants completed a visual search task and auditory N-back task (absent, 1, 2, 3) in isolation or together via a within-subjects, randomized, and factorial paradigm. We assessed cross-modal influence using summary statistics, a nonparametric metric of efficiency, and complementary evidence accumulation models. As predicted, we found dual-task deficits in both tasks when paired, and further declines in performance with increased task load. Further, our modeling results indicated a reconfiguration in decision-making architecture as cross-modal load increased—lower response caution in one task (thresholds) to compensate for the unavoidable degradation of processing quality in another (drift rates). Overall, our results suggest that dual-task capacity limits not only govern the amount of information humans can process, but impose (in)stable decision-making strategies across competing resources streams.
summaryZh: 两任务配对完成时均出现双任务缺陷，且随任务负荷增加表现进一步下降。 建模结果显示，随跨通道负荷增加，决策架构发生重构：一个任务降低反应谨慎性（阈值）以补偿另一任务加工质量（漂移率）不可避免的下降。 作者据此提出双任务容量限制不仅约束可加工的信息量，还在竞争的资源流之间施加（不）稳定的决策策略。
